relationships.subject: nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: In both male and female mice, nerve injury decreases PVINs' output via mechanisms that are not fully understood.

relationships.subject: SK channels
relationships.evidence_quote: tonic firing PVINs from naive male mice become adaptive when exposed to an SK channel activator, and (2) adapting PVINs from nerve-injured male mice return to tonic firing on SK channel blockade

relationships.subject: intracellular calcium
relationships.evidence_quote: a depletion of cytosolic calcium buffer allows for the rapid accumulation of intracellular calcium through the active membranes, which in turn potentiates SK channels and impedes spike generation

relationships.subject: dorsal horn parvalbumin interneurons
relationships.evidence_quote: The loss of their inhibitory tone leads to neuropathic symptoms, such as mechanical allodynia

key_findings: After nerve injury, spinal dorsal horn PV interneurons from male mice switch from tonic to adaptive firing, reducing their output.

Modeling and pharmacology indicate this switch arises from increased SK channel contribution enabled by impaired calcium buffering; SK activation made naive PVINs adaptive and SK blockade restored tonic firing in injured PVINs.
